title: Where to eat
intro: A note on tourist-trap avoidance: the generic “best restaurants in Sedona” lists skew toward the Uptown strip closest to hotels — this guide deliberately routes through spots local guides actually name as where residents eat.

items.name: Wildcraft Cafe
items.hours: ⚠ Varies by day of week — confirm before you go
items.why: Health-conscious, organic, vegan/paleo/gluten-free options — an easy local breakfast or lunch that isn't a hotel buffet.

items.name: Elote Cafe
items.why: Sedona's most in-demand table — bold, elevated Southwestern and Mexican cooking.
items.crowd_tip: Reserve ahead, especially on a weekend — it's not a reliable walk-in.

items.name: El Rincon
items.why: Traditional Mexican food without the elevated price or the wait — a good backup if Elote is booked out.

items.name: Tamaliza
items.why: Traditional Mexican food without the elevated price or the wait — a good backup if Elote is booked out.

items.name: Coffee Pot Restaurant
items.why: A west-side local institution for 30+ years — a straightforward, unpretentious breakfast spot.
